text:
tess: Quick sync — thinking about a small refactor to make inference telemetry SLO-aware and reduce cost leakage. Proposal: a "slim-bridge" at ingest that collapses cross-service trace fanout, carries a cheap billing-key hint, and lets downstream samplers decide exact retention.

leo: sketch? curious how this avoids double-counting cost when traces fan out to async workers.

tess: high level: 1) at ingress, attach a minimal envelope with: tenant, route-hash, cheap-billing-hint (not authoritative). 2) immediately route a single compact envelope to observability pipeline (no fanout). 3) downstreams (async workers, batch jobs) keep local logs but only the enriched canonical trace resumes if sampler marks it for retention.

marco: so we stop sending full spans to observability for every fanout path? how do we debug failures then?

tess: we still emit local debug logs to the app log system (low retention). The canonical trace that goes into long-term store is the slim-bridge envelope + optional sampled spans. Debugging: if you need full path, you can trigger a per-request trace debug flag (via route header) which forces capture.

sasha: i like. two concerns: (A) how do we guarantee billing attribution if sampling decisions happen after fanout? (B) compatibility with existing enrichment hooks.

ingrid: for (A) we could keep a lightweight cost-token that flows with the envelope and is sticky across retries. The token is resolved to a billing key in the billing backend asynchronously. We only use the token to increment provisional counters so metrics reflect load even for unsampled traces.

marco: token sounds fine but we need to avoid token explosion (cardinality). Maybe route-hash + tenant prefix is enough for preliminary bucketing.

leo: For (B) what about enrichment that currently relies on full span context available at ingress? those enrichers are sync today.

obs-bot: Note: enrichment-sidecar feature flag currently set to ON for canary orgs.

tess: Plan: maintain a small pre-enrich phase in the slim-bridge that runs cheap attribute extraction (no downstream lookups). Heavy enrichers (geo, tenant-lookup) are deferred to the canonical pipeline only when sampler keeps the trace. That reduces cost.

sasha: How does this affect queryability? e.g., cost-explorer wants per-route cost with fine granularity, we must ensure the canonical store has enough keys.

ingrid: canonical traces will include resolved billing-key when available; for cases where resolve is async we keep the cost-token and a mapping table that materializes later. Querying layer can join on token -> billing-key. There will be a short window with provisional buckets.

marco: edge case: multi-model inference where a single request fans out to N model containers. We might tag route-hash with model-id in the token to avoid undercounting per-model cost.

leo: operationally, what are the rollout steps? sounds like infra + runtime + console changes.

tess: rollout proposal: (1) implement slim-bridge ingest in a feature-flagged path (runtime + proxy) that emits compact envelopes; (2) add token plumbing and join table in billing service; (3) add sampler hook in canonical pipeline; (4) canary with low-traffic tenants; (5) increase rollout and flip default.

sasha: testing: we should have a simple end-to-end smoke that verifies 1) no cost double-counting, 2) ability to force-capture, 3) token resolve idempotence.

ingrid: also add dashboards showing provisional vs resolved billing over time so finance can approve the switch.

marco: one more: retention policy — sampled canonical traces are the only ones kept long-term. non-sampled slim envelopes are TTL'd quickly. Make that explicit in docs.

tess: agreed. I'll draft an RFC appendix for the slim-bridge pattern with sequence diagrams and a small compatibility shim for existing enrichers.

leo: sounds good. can you include a fallback plan that re-enables full fanout if we detect >1% missing critical traces in canary?

tess: yes — fallback circuit: on canary, run both full fanout + slim-bridge in parallel, compare sampling coverage; if coverage drops or cost attribution diverges by >1% we revert by routing to full fanout. Will document thresholds.

sasha: ok, assign follow-ups?

tess: follow-ups: 1) tess + marco: sequence diagrams + sample code for envelope (ETA 2d). 2) ingrid + leo: billing token design + join-table + dashboards (ETA 4d). 3) sasha: integration tests + canary plan (ETA 3d). 4) ops-bot: add feature-flag gate and rollout automation.

obs-bot: Created task: OBS-3921 "slim-bridge ingest prototype" assigned to tess,marco,ingrid,sasha.

marco: thanks. quick note — include a sample envelope proto in the RFC. maybe like:
```
message SlimEnvelope {
  string request_id = 1;
  string tenant = 2;
  string route_hash = 3;
  string cost_token = 4; // low-card hint
  repeated KeyValue attrs = 5; // tiny set (<=8)
}
```

tess: perfect. I'll post the RFC doc link when it's up. tagging @sasha @ingrid @marco for visibility. :metal:

sasha: looking forward to the draft.

leo: thanks all.
